justification: Sutherland's website returns 403 to the monitor (and to Zyte), so its DCP chapters could never be fetched, stored or extracted; 28 number rules cite them. A person can download the PDF in a browser. This feeds that file into the monitor's own write path so the PDF enters through the pipeline (versioned R2 copy, registry hash, needs_extraction, recorder) instead of by hand. It also fixes a real bug: a content_hash with r2_current_path NULL was treated as unchanged forever.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The r2_path fix is reverted (if new_hash == stored_hash:) - measured: 2 of 5 fail. A manual run calls the council (head_request/download_pdf/hub scraper are set to raise). A non-PDF is stored. A second chapter is written.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Measured 2026-11-02: with 'if new_hash == stored_hash:' restored, test_known_case_hash_set_but_no_file_is_stored_and_queued and test_a_normal_run_still_downloads_a_hash_with_no_file failed (2 failed, 3 passed).

pre_impl.existing_data: Registry rows for both Sutherland chapters already hold content_hash 5aabb8ad... (ch2) and 0e4555bb... (ch4) with r2_current_path NULL; the browser downloads match both byte for byte.
pre_impl.prior_art: add_new_chapter.py, confirm_chapter.py, dcp_extract_changed.py and r2_monitor.py have no local-file option; the unblocker decision (meta-eval-web-unblocker-apis-2026-10-24) was tried: Zyte 520 Website Ban twice.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I assumed the monitor would store a file whose hash was already recorded. It would not: equal hashes took the unchanged branch even with no stored file, which is why Sutherland was stuck.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new write path. The existing per-chapter body of run_monitor does every write; the change only swaps where the bytes come from and adds a key filter.

functions.name: run_monitor
functions.input: council filter plus manual_key (a registered chapter_key) and manual_file (a local PDF path)
functions.output: the usual results dict with only that chapter processed and no hub scrape
functions.if_none: manual_key and manual_file default to None, which is the unchanged daily behaviour

functions.name: read_manual_pdf
functions.input: the filesystem path of a PDF a person downloaded in a browser
functions.output: a tuple of the raw bytes and an empty headers dict
functions.if_none: a missing path raises FileNotFoundError and the chapter is reported failed, nothing written

values.value: dry run: ch2 and ch4 would upload to source-pdfs/dcps/sutherland_shire/v2.0-2026-11-02/
values.if_missing: no evidence the real registry rows take the store path

break_it.scenario: An HTML error page saved with a .pdf name
break_it.what_happens: _assert_pdf_body raises before any upload or registry write
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated in code on this branch: read_manual_pdf calls _assert_pdf_body, which raises on a body not starting %PDF or under MIN_PDF_BYTES
break_it.how: read_manual_pdf calls _assert_pdf_body, which raises on a body not starting %PDF or under MIN_PDF_BYTES

break_it.scenario: A stale or wrong file is fed for the chapter
break_it.what_happens: its hash differs, so it takes the CHANGED path: a new version is stored, linked controls are flagged chapter_pdf_changed and the chapter is queued for extraction review
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated in code on this branch: the differing hash routes to the existing CHANGED branch, which sets needs_extraction and flags linked controls for review
break_it.how: the differing hash routes to the existing CHANGED branch, which sets needs_extraction and flags linked controls for review

break_it.what_happens: argparse stops the run with an error before any connection is made
break_it.mitigated: Mitigated in code on this branch: main() calls parser.error unless --chapter-key, --from-file and --council are all given together
break_it.how: main() calls parser.error unless --chapter-key, --from-file and --council are all given together

mutation_analysis: Reverting the r2_path condition makes the known-case test and the source test fail (2/5), run not reasoned. The 'only the named chapter' test fails if the key filter is removed because two registry writes appear.
residual_risk: A manually fed chapter is not watched: the council still blocks the monitor, so an amendment is only seen when someone downloads again. The 403s stay visible in waf_blocked. The fake-DB test checks the SQL parameters, not a real database.

post_merge.db_reset: No schema change. After merge: run the two manual intakes live (writes R2 + registry for 2 chapters), then the normal extract-to-review stage.
post_merge.other_repo: None; the Railway dcp-monitor cron runs without the new flags and behaves as before.
post_merge.manual_verify: Run the two intakes live, then select r2_current_path, content_hash, needs_extraction from dcp_chapter_registry for both Sutherland chapters and check the R2 objects' sha256.
